1.sofaString: 192	Pt, ****, is a 14 month old female[FP1], diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy and cardiogenic shock[FP2] who is being referred by ******* ****** APRN for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's parents and review of the medical records.   SW spent 60 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, ****, resides with her parents, grandparents, and siblings in a single story home[FP3]. The home has well water and window a/c.  They do not drink the water, but use bottled water[FP4].   They have 3 dogs, 2 lizards, and some chickens[FP5]. There is no smoking in the home[FP6].       Demographics:  Mother: ********* *******  DOB: **/*/****  Age: 31  Education:  High School diploma[FP7]  Employment:  Not employed[FP8]. Disabled, receives SSI[FP9].  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ***** *******  DOB: **/**/****  Age: 30  Education: 11th grade education[FP10]  Employment: Self-employed[FP11] doing ******** and odd jobs[FP12]  Phone: ***-***-**** (cell)     Siblings:  Brother: ***** ******* **, Age 9  Sister: **** *******, Age 6     Support systems:  Parents have been married for 6 years.  They have been together for much longer however[FP13].  They are currently rotating turns being at bedside due to ******* visitor restrictions.  The grandparents are currently assisting with the other children[FP14].        The parents disclose that their extended family are supportive. Grandparents on both sides are local to them, and involved.  In addition, the paternal aunts and ****** are nearby and also a support to the family[FP15].      Neither parent has a working vehicle. However, they are able to use the grandmother's vehicle when needed[FP16]. Both parents report having a driver's license.  They state that transportation here is not a problem, as they are able to use grandmother's car or have multiple other friends and support persons who can assist them[FP17] with transportation[FP18].        Both parents report that they are *********. Neither report any objection to blood products, transfusions, etc.      Course of illness:        **** is a 14 month old female[FP19].  She was born at 36 weeks 3 days via repeat C Section.  She was diagnosed with Persistent Left ******** Vena Cava to Coronary Sinus;  Aorta without narrowing with tiny Patent Ductus Arteriosus[FP20]. She was discharged at 3 days old. She was recommended for outpatient follow up with peds cardiology within one month of discharge. However, she was not seen until almost 6 months of age.  She was doing well, and was not recommended for any additional cardiology follow-up unless she became symptomatic.     She reportedly had a fairly normal first year of life, with the exception of frequent emesis and poor growth.  She presented to OSH the day prior to admission here with fatigue, decreased feeding, decreased urination, and increased work of breathing. She was also found to be anemic, and was given a large PRBC transfusion.  She was then transferred to our hospital for further management.     She was found to have severely dilated LV with severely depressed function. She was also intubated due to worsening respiratory status and increased lactic acidosis. She is now being evaluated for possible escalation of care to include ECMO, VAD, and transplant.        Financial Situation:     **** is covered by Medicaid ******** insurance[FP21].  She has not yet been applied for SSI, but the family is interested in doing so[FP22].  The family receives food ******. They are not currently receiving WIC because mom states she does not feel comfortable going to the WIC office with the current ******* situation[FP23].  Mom receives SSI[FP24].  In addition, dad works to support the family.       Family History:     The family reports that both of the older siblings had 'large hearts' as babies, but grew out of this. They report that **** was on a liquid medication for her heart rate, but they cannot remember what it was.  They state she no longer requires any meds.  Mom is diagnosed with diabetes. She states she controls it primarily by diet, but does take insulin if she has a large meal or consumes a large amount of sugar.  She states she only checks her blood sugar when she feels symptomatic.  Documentation indicates 'poorly controlled' diabetes during the pregnancy with ****, leading to an admission for DKA at 30 weeks gestation.  Mom also reports that she had a tubal ligation after giving birth to ****. Dad denies any medical history for himself or his side of the family.     Mom also reports that she has been on disability since age 4[FP25]. She states this is because she has a hard time 'comprehending'. She states it is like a learning disability[FP26], but more than just that. She states she is able to read, but would benefit from instructions verbally as well as in writing.     Both parents report a history of depression, anxiety, and 'bipolar'. Neither are currently on any psychotropic meds for this. Both report having been on psychotropic meds in the past however[FP27].  They state belief that the meds were not useful. Neither report having participated in counseling previously[FP28].  Mom admits that this admission has been stressful. She states she cannot look at **** without crying[FP29].  She states it is hard to see her lying there intubated, when she had previously been active.  SW validated that this is a traumatic experience, and encouraged both to consider counseling[FP30] to assist with coping with the challenges of transplant.  Both parents were encouraged to participate in self-care and is caring for their relationship.[FP31]      Dad reports a history of using marijuana. He states he only infrequently does this now, as he has 'grown up'. He states he does not use in the home, but does occasionally smoke with some of his friends. No other substance use was reported by either parent.[FP32]     Dad reports a history of arrests.  He has been arrested for driving without a valid driver's license. He has also been arrested for charges of battery[FP33] on mom[FP34], during her first pregnancy.  Both report that this 'was a long time ago' and state they get along better now. They deny any current DV problems[FP35].     Both parents report that they have investigated by DCF on several occasions as well.  They state that they have been reported for neglect[FP36]. However, they state this is always unsubstantiated when the investigator meets with them and visits their home.       Adherence:  There are several concerns for adherence documented[FP37].  **** had a prenatal ultrasound that was concerning for dilated coronary sinus with slight RV predominance, suspicion for persistent LSVC and need to rule out COA. She was referred to pediatric fetal cardiology several times for further evaluation of this. However, this was never done[FP38]. In addition, there is concern that mom did not keep her own medical appointments and care during the pregnancy, and her diabetes was 'poorly controlled'[FP39]. This led to an admission for DKA.       After **** was born, she was referred for follow up with pediatric cardiology at 1 month of life. However, she did not follow up until age 5 months[FP40]. There is also concern related to her failure to thrive. She was at 0.06 % on the growth chart for weight on the day of admission. Her length is at 14%.  It is unclear if this was related to medical issues with her heart, or lack of nutrition[FP41]. She was primarily receiving breast milk, as she was not really tolerating solid foods.     Parents report that they are a little nervous at the thought of having to administer medications on a strict schedule[FP42].  However, they believe they will be able to do so.         Parents are demonstrating bonding with **** by being at bedside with her as much as possible.  Both parents appear ********* to her[FP43].          Assessment and recommendations:     Mom disclosed that transplant is a new concept to them, and she is holding onto belief that **** will get better and not need transplant. However, she states her main priority is that **** survives, and she would like to do transplant if that is her only hope[FP44].  She states she cannot have any other children, and cannot fathom life without **** in it.  Dad states he is also hopeful that she will not need a new heart, but is open to moving forward if it is needed[FP45].             IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  2  Family Background & Social Support -  2  Financial/Insurance  - 2  Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 3  Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  3  Adherence - 3  Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2  Health Literacy -  2  Coping Skills - 2     Total:  21 Moderate/High Risk       The family scores as moderate/high risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant. Primary concerns are past history of poor adherence[FP46] with medical care, history with DCF[FP47], history of DV[FP48], and limited financial resources[FP49].   Protective factors include the family's ******* about these past concerns, the family's current involvement in patient's admission[FP50], and adequate support persons[FP51].     Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  Use teachback method to confirm understanding. Provide information both verbally and in writing.   *Provide fundraising resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to transplant   * Assist family with resources to assist in coping with potentially lengthy admission  *Assist in connecting parents with counseling resources[FP52]   [FP1]gender[FP2]ACC Healthcare[FP3]Living Condition[FP4]Living Supply[FP5]Living Condition[FP6]Smoking[FP7]Education General[FP8]Employment Status[FP9]Insurance[FP10]Education General[FP11]Employment Status[FP12]Occupation[FP13]Social Cohesion[FP14]Social Support[FP15]Social Support[FP16]Social Support[FP17]Social Support[FP18]Financial Constraint[FP19]Gender[FP20]ACC Healthcare[FP21]Insurance[FP22]Insurance[FP23]Poverty[FP24]Insurance[FP25]Poverty[FP26]Mental Health[FP27]Mental Health (Historical)[FP28]Mental Health (Historical)[FP29]Mental Health[FP30]Mental Health[FP31]Reccomendations[FP32]Drug Abuse[FP33]Legal Involvement[FP34]IPV[FP35]IPV[FP36]Abuse[FP37]Adherence[FP38]Adherence[FP39]Adherence[FP40]Adherence[FP41]Living Supply[FP42]Adherence[FP43]Social Cohesion[FP44]Literacy[FP45]Literacy[FP46]Adherence[FP47]Abuse[FP48]IPV[FP49]Poverty[FP50]Social Cohesion[FP51]Social Support[FP52]Reccomendations
